# Sirach Chapter 26 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 26 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

**26:1** Blessed is the man whose wife is good; he will live twice as long.

**26:2** A capable wife is her husband's joy; he will finish out his years in peace.

**26:3** A good wife is a precious gift; she is given to those who fear the LORD.

**26:4** Rich or poor, his heart is content, his face always bright.

**26:5** Three things made my heart tremble, and a fourth left me face-down on the ground: city gossip, a mob assembling, and a false charge — all three are worse than death.

**26:6** But the bitterest grief of all is a wife who is jealous of a rival, and a tongue that can't keep quiet about anything.

**26:7** A bad wife is a yoke that galls the neck; getting hold of her is like grabbing a scorpion.

**26:8** A wife who drinks too much stirs up enormous trouble and won't bother to hide her own shame.

**26:9** An unchaste woman advertises herself in how she looks around; you can read it in her eyes.

**26:10** Watch your headstrong daughter closely — she'll take any opening she gets.

**26:11** Keep an eye on that roving glance of hers; don't be surprised when she goes wrong.

**26:12** She's like a thirsty traveler opening her mouth to drink from every puddle; she parks herself at every post and opens her quiver to every arrow.

**26:13** A gracious wife is her husband's delight; her wisdom puts health in his bones.

**26:14** A quiet wife is a gift from God; no price can be put on a disciplined character.

**26:15** A modest wife is grace doubled over; no scales can weigh a self-controlled soul.

**26:16** Like the sun coming up over the LORD's high places — that is the beauty of a good wife presiding over a well-run household.

**26:17** Like the lamp gleaming on the sacred lampstand — that is a beautiful face on a graceful figure.

**26:18** Like gold columns on silver pedestals — that is beautiful feet set on steady ankles.

**26:19** My child, guard your health and the vitality of your youth; don't give your strength away to strangers.

**26:20** Find the best land in the whole country and sow it with your own seed — trust in the quality of your own children.

**26:21** The children who survive you will be great, for they will have confidence in their good breeding.

**26:22** A hired woman is worth no more than a spit; but a married woman is a tower of death for any man who lays a hand on her.

**26:23** A lawless woman will end up with a lawless man; a woman who fears God will be given to a man who fears God.

**26:24** The shameless woman will be put to shame over and over; the woman of honor will be honored in return.

**26:25** The lawless woman has no sense of shame; the woman of honor respects her husband.

**26:26** A wife who respects her husband earns everyone's respect; a wife who looks down on him in pride is known by everyone as godless. A loud woman is like a trumpet blaring at every disturbance; any man on the warpath will stop to listen.

**26:27** Two things make me grieve, and a third makes me furious: a soldier ground down by poverty; wise people treated like garbage; and someone who turns their back on right and chooses sin — the LORD has a sword waiting for that person.

**26:28** [A merchant can barely avoid cutting corners; a dealer will not come away from it with clean hands.]

**26:29** [Many people have gone wrong chasing profit; if you're always trying to get more, you end up looking away from what matters.]
